name: The Fool
upright: A vetted, trained user who spots the lure, reports it and becomes the organization's first line of defense.
reversed: Unvetted hires, unchecked insiders and one careless click: the human who opens the gate for every attacker.
vision: A traveler strides toward a cliff edge, eyes on the sun. At the trailhead behind them, a gatekeeper who has read their whole past in the lines of their palm waves goodbye, and over their shoulder swings a bindle stuffed with signed promises. A cloud lowers a white rose on a fishhook. A small dog barks, and the traveler stops, one heel on the rim. Three signposts line the path: an eye that says look, a hand that says how, a book that says why. Every spring the traveler leaves their boots with a stranger for two weeks, and the stranger walks the same path, turning over every stone.
decode: One heel on the cliff edge, eyes on the sun → the user: the weakest link and, once trained, the first line of defense.
A white rose on a fishhook; the dog whose bark halts the step → phishing lures look harmless; simulated phishing trains users to pause and report.
The gatekeeper reading the palm, the bindle of signed promises → background checks before hire; an NDA signed at onboarding that binds even after leaving.
Signposts of eye, hand and book → awareness changes what people notice; training teaches how to do the job; education builds the deeper why.
A stranger walks the path in the traveler's boots for two weeks → mandatory vacation: someone else does the work and can uncover fraud.
facts: Mandatory vacation (often one to two weeks) is a detective control: a substitute doing the job can uncover fraud. Job rotation both deters and detects it.
At termination, disable access at the same time as, or just before, the person is told; then collect badges and keys and use the exit interview to restate the NDA.
Hiring starts with a job description that defines the role's access; screening and background checks follow, and the NDA is signed before access is granted.
trap: The collective keeps mistaking awareness for training. Posters and banners make people notice (awareness); teaching staff to do their jobs securely is training; education is deeper study for a security career.
